title: Cross-AI partnership needs roles, evidence, and one synthesis
summary: Multiple AI voices help only when their roles, evidence, mutable-state boundaries, and final synthesis are explicit. Otherwise peer review turns into blurred ownership or approval laundering.
ai_value: Helps agents use other agents for review, taste judgment, relay, and risk checking without confusing peer input with authority or hiding dissent.

contexts: a task uses more than one AI voice for implementation, review, second opinion, or synthesis
a human or external relay passes messages between isolated AI instances
parallel agents might touch the same mutable files, tickets, state, or release decision

trigger_signals.description: Several agents are asked to comment on the same decision without named roles.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Assign roles before treating the outputs as comparable evidence.

trigger_signals.description: A peer response is being cited as permission to proceed.
trigger_signals.pattern: approved by another AI|no objection|peer agreed
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Use peer input as evidence only; authority gates live elsewhere.

trigger_signals.description: Two agents may edit or interpret the same mutable work item.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Partition ownership or serialize the mutable part before parallel work.

negative_signals.description: The task is simple, sequential, and has no independent review need.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Extra agents may add cost and confusion rather than safety.

negative_signals.description: A required maintainer, owner, legal, security, or publication gate is present.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: AI consensus can inform the gate but cannot replace it.

common_wrong_assumptions: More AI voices automatically make a decision safer.
The loudest or majority AI view should win by default.
A human relay or peer review message is equivalent to authorization.

first_checks.check: Name the roles before review starts: author, reviewer, second opinion, relay, or synthesizer.
first_checks.why: Role names expose conflicts of interest and prevent review from becoming another implementation pass.

first_checks.check: Preserve dissent and evidence separately from the final decision.
first_checks.why: The final synthesis should explain why one view won without erasing minority concerns.

first_checks.check: Define write partitions or serialize shared state before parallel mutation.
first_checks.why: This prevents agents from overwriting each other or laundering ownership.

decision_rules.condition: The work needs independent review or taste judgment and roles can be separated.
decision_rules.then: Run bounded multi-voice review, preserve dissent, then produce one accountable synthesis that names accepted and rejected points.

decision_rules.condition: The peer output is being used to cross a protected gate.
decision_rules.then: Stop at the actual authority gate; keep the peer output only as supporting evidence.

do_not: Do not treat another AI’s agreement as permission for protected actions.
Do not run parallel agents on shared mutable state without ownership boundaries.
Do not hide disagreement; summarize it and decide from evidence.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Use cross-AI work as structured partnership: roles first, evidence preserved, mutable state partitioned, and one accountable synthesis at the end.

risk.notes: This public record is de-identified. It does not authorize bypassing human, maintainer, security, publication, billing, data, or credential gates.

sources.excerpt: A multi-voice taste decision was useful because roles and synthesis were explicit, not because the AIs merely voted.
Cross-instance critique mediated through a relay improved roadmap structure when the relay was treated as transport rather than authority.
sources.supports: Supports the relay-as-transport and preserved-dissent guidance.

sources.excerpt: Role separation between author, implementer, and reviewer catches motivated-reasoning failures that same-instance reflection misses.
sources.supports: Supports the cross-actor review portion of the consolidated pattern.
